## Strategy guide

Draft from SCPT episode 358, “Super Yssaril Tribes Guide” (published 2024-07-03). Ruleset compatibility is unreviewed. The complete faster-whisper small.en transcript is a verified ASR draft; timestamps point to overlapping speech, but proper nouns are noisy.

### Strategic thesis

#### C01

**Advice:** The action-card engine compounds over time: cards answer problems across movement, combat, economy, technology, and agendas, while Scheming lets Yssaril prune toward useful options. The hosts describe a tailored late-game toolkit, not a guaranteed win.

**When it applies:** Best over a longer game; results still depend on cards, board, scoring pace, and player decisions.

**Evidence:** 43:39.81–43:47.65 (s000853); 43:50.47–43:54.09 (s000855); 45:12.99–45:15.07 (s000880); 45:16.77–45:19.03 (s000882).

### Priorities and options

#### C02

**Advice:** The opening has two carriers, a cruiser, two fighters, five infantry, and a home PDS. The hosts call this broadly useful but describe the early ground position as thin until mechs can be deployed.

**When it applies:** Expand with the fleet while accounting for the action cards required to place mechs.

**Evidence:** 13:27.65–13:33.71 (s000245); 13:33.73–13:39.11 (s000246); 25:11.83–25:15.89 (s000492); 25:24.61–25:28.01 (s000495).

#### C03

**Advice:** Neural Motivator is a natural starting technology: it draws an extra action card, and Scheming adds a card when drawing then permits a discard. That supports selection rather than a simple draw-and-keep pattern.

**When it applies:** Most useful when there are weak cards to prune or several new choices; it does not promise a particular card.

**Evidence:** 13:48.71–13:50.13 (s000251); 19:13.79–19:20.13 (s000365); 19:20.15–19:23.79 (s000366); 19:49.75–19:56.21 (s000380); 20:00.01–20:06.69 (s000382).

#### C04

**Advice:** Politics secondary is attractive because additional cards can build a large hand without the ordinary limit forcing Yssaril to prune down to seven. The hosts describe card draw as positive momentum.

**When it applies:** Not an automatic follow; command tokens, timing, and card utility still matter.

**Evidence:** 22:06.25–22:11.65 (s000417); 22:23.41–22:25.93 (s000422); 22:36.31–22:40.21 (s000428).

#### C05

**Advice:** Stall Tactics turns an action-card discard into an action-phase stall without passing. Using it can also trigger mech deployment, giving the stall an additional payoff and an early deterrent.

**When it applies:** Use when delaying is valuable and a mech can be deployed on a controlled planet.

**Evidence:** 17:05.55–17:08.75 (s000319); 17:15.55–17:19.21 (s000324); 24:47.63–24:54.39 (s000485); 24:54.41–24:59.49 (s000486); 25:00.41–25:02.69 (s000488).

#### C06

**Advice:** Mechs cover some early ground weakness: opponents may avoid attacking a planet Yssaril can hold, even when its ships are weaker. The hosts also say killing Yssaril carriers may be worthwhile to force spending.

**When it applies:** This is deterrence rather than immunity; an opponent may target ships or force expenditure.

**Evidence:** 25:24.61–25:28.01 (s000495); 25:31.53–25:34.25 (s000497); 25:41.31–25:45.19 (s000500); 25:45.21–25:48.95 (s000501).

#### C07

**Advice:** The flagship’s two movement and ability to pass through enemy-occupied systems can enable an early surprise, such as reaching Mecatol Rex. Light/Wave Deflectors or In the Silence of Space can make its special movement redundant.

**When it applies:** Build around this only when map and timing provide a target; the hosts also value its combat profile.

**Evidence:** 23:21.85–23:22.87 (s000451); 23:34.63–23:38.07 (s000459); 23:38.09–23:39.95 (s000460); 24:24.77–24:28.41 (s000477); 23:57.91–24:00.11 (s000468); 24:15.17–24:17.65 (s000474).

#### C08

**Advice:** Spy Net lets a player look at Yssaril’s action cards and take one. The hosts say players often sell or hand over a negotiated card instead of exposing the full choice, and call this common practice potentially contrary to intent.

**When it applies:** Clarify the exchange before trading the note; the hosts question what “look” means and describe a trust convention.

**Evidence:** 25:55.03–26:01.25 (s000505); 26:01.27–26:04.57 (s000506); 26:26.31–26:30.19 (s000515); 26:42.03–26:47.95 (s000518); 28:58.65–29:01.53 (s000571); 29:06.31–29:08.77 (s000574).

#### C09

**Advice:** Ssruu copies another player’s agent text, even if exhausted. The hosts emphasize that this does not grant every other component referenced by that text; Yssaril is still using Ssruu.

**When it applies:** Value depends on agents present and useful timing.

**Evidence:** 30:09.53–30:17.05 (s000595); 31:34.49–31:36.95 (s000615); 31:37.39–31:40.85 (s000616); 31:49.37–31:51.19 (s000621); 31:56.21–31:57.85 (s000625).

#### C10

**Advice:** So Ata unlocks with seven action cards. The hosts say this often arrives around round three or four because Yssaril may spend cards on mechs, and advise against warping play around the commander.

**When it applies:** Track the threshold while balancing card use and mech deployment; the speakers admit it is easy to forget.

**Evidence:** 32:45.85–32:50.23 (s000643); 33:07.27–33:09.19 (s000651); 33:12.51–33:14.15 (s000653); 33:21.87–33:24.21 (s000656); 33:26.65–33:29.35 (s000658).

#### C11

**Advice:** After an opponent activates a system with Yssaril units, So Ata can inspect that player’s cards, promissory notes, or secret objectives. The hosts usually favor secret objectives as the most useful information, but note that a late card search can matter.

**When it applies:** Reactive trigger; choose information by game state.

**Evidence:** 33:31.45–33:33.39 (s000660); 33:37.59–33:40.65 (s000663); 33:41.15–33:43.19 (s000664); 34:03.53–34:07.95 (s000669); 34:09.49–34:11.69 (s000671); 34:28.37–34:29.41 (s000680).

#### C12

**Advice:** Kyver’s hero makes each opponent show a card, then lets Yssaril take it or force three random discards. The hosts see little choice for Yssaril: even an unwanted card can be a stall, while discarding three may remove valuable options.

**When it applies:** They identify an exception when the leader has few cards and Yssaril wants to strip them.

**Evidence:** 36:00.31–36:07.35 (s000714); 36:07.37–36:12.33 (s000715); 36:12.35–36:18.39 (s000716); 36:21.69–36:26.43 (s000718); 36:48.75–36:53.83 (s000724); 37:32.19–37:33.47 (s000735).

#### C13

**Advice:** Transparasteel Plating can stop players who have passed from playing action cards during Yssaril’s turn. It is situational but accessible from the starting green technology, useful when late responses matter.

**When it applies:** Compare with Hyper Metabolism by economy and whether opponents hold important cards.

**Evidence:** 38:46.53–38:48.05 (s000755); 38:52.63–38:54.41 (s000759); 38:54.63–38:58.43 (s000760); 39:35.71–39:40.17 (s000774); 40:00.43–40:05.45 (s000784); 40:23.93–40:28.93 (s000790).

#### C14

**Advice:** The preferred tech engine centers on Bio-Stims and Magi-on Implants, with Gravity Drive for movement. Bio-Stims can ready Magi-on for another use that round; the hosts describe the resulting card access as powerful.

**When it applies:** Tech intensive; shift with skips, economy, timing, or urgent movement.

**Evidence:** 40:44.57–40:51.57 (s000794); 40:51.59–40:57.63 (s000795); 41:09.01–41:15.85 (s000798); 41:15.87–41:23.41 (s000799); 63:01.49–63:08.15 (s001265); 63:15.41–63:17.63 (s001268); 63:27.65–63:28.93 (s001272).

#### C15

**Advice:** The no-skip outline adds a choice between Hyper Metabolism and Transparasteel, then Magi-on, followed by blue access such as Dark Energy Tap or Antimass into Gravity Drive and possibly Carrier II, Fleet Logistics, and Light/Wave.

**When it applies:** Adaptable route, not fixed order; options may remain useful through round five.

**Evidence:** 64:28.37–64:33.93 (s001298); 64:34.45–64:41.25 (s001299); 64:42.17–64:45.55 (s001300); 64:48.83–64:52.01 (s001302); 64:56.21–64:57.99 (s001305); 64:58.61–65:01.21 (s001306); 65:01.75–65:03.45 (s001307); 65:09.15–65:12.81 (s001311).

#### C16

**Advice:** With a green skip, Yssaril can omit Hyper Metabolism or Transparasteel; a blue skip may bypass Dark Energy Tap or Antimass for Gravity Drive. Dreadnought II with a yellow skip is mentioned as nonessential.

**When it applies:** Use skips to shorten research; pursue upgrades when objectives or cards justify them.

**Evidence:** 65:37.81–65:44.09 (s001319); 65:44.11–65:48.61 (s001320); 65:48.63–65:53.11 (s001321); 65:53.71–65:57.01 (s001322); 65:57.03–66:02.11 (s001323); 66:36.17–66:39.27 (s001341).

#### C17

**Advice:** The hosts usually avoid red and yellow technologies and favor green and blue. They prefer Carrier II over Fighter II, while acknowledging the preference is personal; Fighter Prototype could make Fighter II appealing.

**When it applies:** Pivot for an objective, slice, or card; several upgrade objectives can justify a detour.

**Evidence:** 66:49.39–66:50.77 (s001350); 66:43.99–66:45.89 (s001345); 67:26.37–67:29.59 (s001361); 67:29.61–67:34.45 (s001362); 67:51.11–67:52.13 (s001369).

#### C18

**Advice:** The hosts first rate round-one Leadership mid-tier, then raise it to high-mid because following Politics can start card flow and offer an early-useful card. Spending an action card to deploy a mech can also create an opening deterrent.

**When it applies:** This describes benefits of following; taking Leadership is not universally best.

**Evidence:** 52:09.43–52:10.49 (s001019); 52:14.47–52:16.05 (s001021); 52:17.81–52:22.19 (s001022); 52:23.99–52:27.01 (s001024); 52:30.05–52:31.87 (s001027); 52:34.35–52:35.39 (s001029).

#### C19

**Advice:** Trade is a strong pick because Yssaril wants technology and plastic. The guide also recommends following Trade when cut out, collecting trade goods without begging for access.

**When it applies:** An economic agent can reduce need; draft order and economy matter.

**Evidence:** 59:14.63–59:16.81 (s001169); 59:23.43–59:26.65 (s001172); 59:28.93–59:30.13 (s001174); 59:36.17–59:38.27 (s001178); 59:51.37–59:53.83 (s001186); 59:53.85–59:57.23 (s001187); 52:53.45–52:54.59 (s001039); 52:54.87–52:55.49 (s001040).

#### C20

**Advice:** Diplomacy can refresh a planet for command tokens or technology spending, but is rated mid-tier. The hosts frame the main opening pressure as funding an ambitious tech path.

**When it applies:** Depends on refreshed planet and timing; compare with Trade and Leadership.

**Evidence:** 53:37.55–53:41.97 (s001058); 53:41.99–53:46.97 (s001059); 53:46.99–53:52.09 (s001060); 53:57.93–53:59.89 (s001062); 54:08.31–54:10.27 (s001068).

#### C21

**Advice:** Politics is not usually the round-one pick despite card synergy: free cards are less valuable before Yssaril has room to use them, and Politics alone rarely secures Custodians. It rises if the table denies tech or an agent creates access.

**When it applies:** Take it for deliberate access or timing; distinguish primary from secondary.

**Evidence:** 54:42.93–54:43.61 (s001085); 54:44.33–54:46.27 (s001086); 54:46.37–54:49.27 (s001087); 54:52.81–54:56.09 (s001090); 55:01.39–55:06.53 (s001092); 55:20.43–55:26.63 (s001095); 56:00.47–56:05.75 (s001103); 56:14.73–56:18.39 (s001107).

#### C22

**Advice:** Construction and Warfare are low-priority opening picks. Yssaril has two home structures and can often afford Construction’s secondary; Warfare is left to factions that need its primary unless an objective changes the need.

**When it applies:** Take when structures or a concrete Warfare need matter.

**Evidence:** 57:49.81–57:50.57 (s001141); 57:52.51–57:53.27 (s001143); 57:53.43–57:56.11 (s001144); 57:58.53–58:00.21 (s001146); 60:42.67–60:44.77 (s001201); 60:50.19–60:51.21 (s001204); 60:57.85–61:00.67 (s001207); 61:03.93–61:06.57 (s001210).

#### C23

**Advice:** Bio-Stims can be a useful first technology, while a green-skip opening may double-tech into Bio-Stims and Magi-on. A blue-first route remains possible when movement is urgent.

**When it applies:** Choose by slice, skip, funds, and movement target; early Gravity Drive matters most for Custodians.

**Evidence:** 54:06.79–54:08.29 (s001067); 54:08.31–54:10.27 (s001068); 54:19.65–54:21.67 (s001073); 56:12.63–56:14.31 (s001106); 56:14.73–56:18.39 (s001107); 62:04.33–62:04.81 (s001239); 62:05.33–62:09.39 (s001240).

#### C24

**Advice:** With Hacan present, the hosts describe a “goblin fish” exchange: Ssruu copies Hacan’s agent, Hacan refreshes commodities, and the factions negotiate a trade-good split.

**When it applies:** Requires both agents, cooperation, and a negotiated split.

**Evidence:** 73:37.69–73:39.21 (s001482); 73:44.65–73:49.21 (s001485); 73:51.47–73:53.37 (s001487); 73:53.83–73:56.51 (s001488); 74:45.07–74:47.55 (s001510); 74:47.89–74:51.31 (s001511); 74:54.45–74:56.55 (s001514); 75:37.85–75:41.71 (s001536).

#### C25

**Advice:** Other agents can create an opening spike: Jol-Nar research, Naalu movement for Custodians, and Mahact command-token interaction to expand or reach Custodians are examples.

**When it applies:** Applies only when those factions are present; evaluate actual agent text and timing.

**Evidence:** 77:06.17–77:08.69 (s001576); 77:09.21–77:11.23 (s001577); 77:20.61–77:22.31 (s001586); 77:22.43–77:23.87 (s001587); 77:31.27–77:36.49 (s001591); 77:36.51–77:42.17 (s001592); 78:02.53–78:04.35 (s001598); 78:38.87–78:41.35 (s001619); 78:48.65–78:52.27 (s001622); 79:01.41–79:06.59 (s001625).

#### C26

**Advice:** The hidden hand can support negotiations over shared control objectives because opponents may prefer cooperation to possible spiteful cards. The hosts also advise finding a Support for the Throne partner early, before the table becomes more wary.

**When it applies:** Offer mutual benefit; cooperation and a swap are not assured.

**Evidence:** 89:21.43–89:25.51 (s001859); 89:25.53–89:29.25 (s001860); 89:30.19–89:35.21 (s001861); 89:35.23–89:39.51 (s001862); 89:39.53–89:44.87 (s001863); 94:46.39–94:50.43 (s001970); 95:04.51–95:08.99 (s001978); 95:09.01–95:13.29 (s001979); 95:24.61–95:29.01 (s001982).

#### C27

**Advice:** The hosts describe Yssaril as strong in agendas because riders can steer outcomes and home influence is useful. They single out Public Execution as dangerous because losing cards hurts, and suggest Politics can help bury it.

**When it applies:** Agenda-deck dependent; Yssaril can stack riders on favorable outcomes.

**Evidence:** 83:42.03–83:45.61 (s001715); 83:45.63–83:48.81 (s001716); 83:54.85–83:57.75 (s001720); 84:17.71–84:19.47 (s001729); 84:19.51–84:21.49 (s001730); 85:14.91–85:17.15 (s001756).

#### C28

**Advice:** Yssaril can prepare for many stage-one objectives: mechs support control, the home PDS and influence help with structures, and cards create unusual completion routes. The guide recommends following Construction when rich as a hedge toward structure objectives.

**When it applies:** Preparation, not automatic scoring; objective must appear and requirements remain.

**Evidence:** 85:26.47–85:29.91 (s001763); 85:32.33–85:34.15 (s001765); 85:34.17–85:35.19 (s001766); 85:50.35–85:52.09 (s001773); 86:04.31–86:09.43 (s001780); 86:21.07–86:25.65 (s001784); 86:31.65–86:33.75 (s001788).

#### C29

**Advice:** Technology objectives are a weaker area because deep green and blue may leave fewer unit upgrades. The hosts still consider Fighter II or Carrier II manageable and say a revealed objective can justify another upgrade.

**When it applies:** Partial technology progress is not scoring; check the revealed requirement.

**Evidence:** 86:51.01–86:53.19 (s001798); 86:57.83–86:59.47 (s001801); 86:59.95–87:01.21 (s001802); 87:01.53–87:03.19 (s001803); 87:03.21–87:08.45 (s001804); 87:08.47–87:13.19 (s001805).

#### C30

**Advice:** For late control objectives, the hosts favor waiting until opponents pass, then sequencing card-enabled movement and captures. Yssaril can win through timing and reach instead of a large fleet contest.

**When it applies:** Needs suitable cards, units, movement, and a completable objective; a large hand alone is insufficient.

**Evidence:** 89:50.93–89:54.57 (s001865); 89:54.59–89:59.77 (s001866); 90:00.89–90:04.63 (s001867); 90:18.77–90:24.63 (s001871); 90:44.97–90:49.07 (s001876); 90:56.09–90:58.23 (s001879); 91:04.29–91:07.15 (s001884).

#### C31

**Advice:** Beyond its ability, the flagship is valued as a heavy combat ship. The hosts compare it to two dreadnoughts in one hull and say early Gravity Drive can make a round-two build reach an equidistant system.

**When it applies:** Build when economy, capacity, and target support it; not solely for pass-through.

**Evidence:** 70:07.49–70:13.65 (s001414); 70:13.67–70:19.39 (s001415); 70:19.85–70:24.81 (s001416); 70:24.83–70:28.55 (s001417); 70:29.29–70:32.69 (s001418); 70:32.71–70:36.89 (s001419).

#### C32

**Advice:** Counterplay remains unresolved: opponents should use valuable cards before Kyver takes them, may target Yssaril ships to force spending, and should recognize the hosts offer no reliable answer to late-game power.

**When it applies:** Advice, not a solved counter; hidden cards can change combat.

**Evidence:** 37:56.91–38:04.17 (s000745); 38:04.19–38:10.03 (s000746); 38:13.79–38:18.01 (s000748); 25:41.31–25:45.19 (s000500); 25:45.21–25:48.95 (s000501); 63:45.75–63:47.49 (s001281); 63:47.61–63:50.27 (s001282).

#### C33

**Advice:** High potential is not assured victory: Yssaril still needs favorable circumstances, scoring opportunities, tempo, and a coherent route to ten. A hidden hand may deter attacks, but it does not score points.

**When it applies:** A large hand or partial objective preparation is not a scored point; verify requirements and endgame sequence.

### Component connections

- **ability:stall_tactics → unit:yssaril_mech (enables):** Using Stall Tactics can trigger mech deployment on a controlled planet, if a mech remains available.
- **technology:bs → technology:gd (enables):** The green engine and later movement technology form the guide’s broad research plan, subject to economy and prerequisites.
- **leader:yssarilagent → leader:hacanagent (synergizes-with):** When both factions cooperate, copying Hacan’s agent can help produce a commodity refresh and negotiated split.
- **technology:tp → technology:hm (conflicts-with):** The guide presents these as alternative early green technologies, chosen by economy and tactical need.

### Source limits

The hosts criticize familiar Yssaril play patterns and revise their own ratings during the episode. The summary keeps competing openings: Leadership to follow Politics, early Trade for economy, and a blue-first route when movement matters. These are conditional options, not one fixed pick order.

The guide uses anecdotal table judgments and does not verify current rules, edition compatibility, or engine legality. Component IDs come from the supplied reference. Magi-on Implants is absent there and remains prose-only. The episode separates preparation from scoring: a large hand, likely objective route, or partial technology path does not itself earn a point.

## Combined source guidance

The guide above contains conditional, transcript-cited advice. The pinned documents below add community research and a bot-oriented mid/late-game profile. Their ordered technology/build lists are proposals, not unconditional policy targets. Keep source disagreements and expansion assumptions visible.

**Historical scope:** upstream statements about available factions, engine support, bot behavior and benchmark results describe that source revision; they are not checks of this checkout. Podcast timestamps in upstream notes are approximate and do not share the local transcript verification.

<details><summary>upstream-community — The Yssaril Tribes (`yssaril`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-yssaril-tribes-yssaril) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-yssaril-tribes-yssaril)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home Retillion 2/3 and Shalloq 1/2; start 2 carriers, 1 cruiser, 2 fighters, 5
infantry, PDS, dock; starting tech Neural Motivator; 3 commodities. Stall Tactics (component action:
discard an action card), Scheming (draw one extra, discard one), Crafty (no hand limit). Faction
techs Transparasteel Plating (G) and Mageon Implants (GGG). Agent Ssruu copies every other agent.
Flagship moves through enemy ships. Commander (7 action cards): look at hands/notes/secrets of
players activating your systems.

**Play.** Yssaril's power is time: Stall Tactics lets them act after everyone has passed, so they
take control objectives at the end of the round, out-stall Warfare in round 1, and play big
moves no one can answer ([BGG "Stall Tactics", 2022](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2997040);
[BGG IncrediSteve on Warfare stalling, 2024](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3232040)). The usual
weakness is plastic: low home resources and production. Advice splits: Sarween first and double
dock at home, or blue (Carrier II, Fighter II) plus one AI Development dip; Mageon Implants is "a
trap without a green skip", though Bio-Stims plus Mageon is called terrifying
([BGG "Yssaril: Meta and Strategy", 2020](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2518695);
[BGG 2023](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/3176141)). Sling Relay helps production. Be friendly
(the threat of a full hand deters attacks); Hacan are natural partners. Pick the strategy card that
scores rather than Politics for the extra card (Politics gets taken anyway). With Bio-Stims,
Mageon Implants twice a round is accepted by tables if spread across players; the real edge is
knowing every hand and acting last with full information
([r/ti "Noob question - Yssaril", 2026](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/1uwe8cm/noob_question_yssaril_tribes/);
[r/ti "How to use Mageon Implants", 2026](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/1wqsyro/how_to_use_mageon_implants_with_yssaril/)).

**Strength.** The best win rate in async PoK data (S+, about 26% in 6-player games against a 16.7%
baseline), A in SCPT 2025 (commenters: should be S), row 3 in SCPT 2022.

**Bot feasibility.**
- Stall Tactics as a component action: when the bot has no activation worth `EAGER_WORTH` and
  others have not passed, discard the worst action card instead of passing or making a weak move;
  then act after the others pass. Value high (it is the faction), effort M (component-action hook
  plus "pass order" awareness; the bot needs to know who has passed, which is public).
- Research: Sarween or Gravity Drive first, Carrier II/Fighter II; avoid Mageon without a green
  skip. Effort S.
- Action cards are random today; Yssaril magnify that gap. A minimal "play cards that are clearly
  good now" layer would help every faction, Yssaril most. Effort L.

</details>

<details><summary>upstream-plans — The Yssaril Tribes (`yssaril`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-plans.md#the-yssaril-tribes-yssaril) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/FACTION_PLANS.md#the-yssaril-tribes-yssaril)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

- **Win path**: action cards and secrets; flexible scoring.
- **Kit**: `nm` start; 2 carriers, cruiser, 2 fighters, 5 infantry, PDS. Stall Tactics,
  Scheming, Crafty. `tp` Transparasteel Plating (G), `mi` Mageon Implants (GGG). Flagship
  moves 2 through enemy ships. Commander at 7 action cards.
- **Mid**: carriers and infantry for planet objectives. **Late**: dreadnoughts plus the
  flagship for a decisive move.
- **Tech**: `dxa`, `tp`, `mi`, `st`, `ps`, `sar`, `hm`, `amd|sr`, `cv2`, `dn2`. Key colour
  green.
- **Build**: mid carriers (2), cruisers, mechs; late dreadnoughts (2), flagship.
- **Cards/tokens**: Politics (cards), strategy pool.
- **Pitfalls**: stalling without a payoff; no board presence.

</details>


## Strategy connections

- [Stall Tactics](../components.md#ability-stall-tactics) **enables** [Blackshade Infiltrator](../components.md#unit-yssaril-mech). Using Stall Tactics can trigger mech deployment on a controlled planet, if a mech remains available. Sources: [SCPT 358, 1018.73–1020.91s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 1043.53–1045.65s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 1480.45–1480.83s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 1502.71–1506.53s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
- [Bio-Stims](../components.md#technology-bs) **enables** [Gravity Drive](../components.md#technology-gd). The green engine and later movement technology form the guide’s broad research plan, subject to economy and prerequisites. Sources: [SCPT 358, 2428.95–2434.81s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 2503.63–2508.67s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 3781.49–3788.15s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 3862.55–3868.35s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
- [Ssruu](../components.md#leader-yssarilagent) **synergizes-with** [Carth of Golden Sands](../components.md#leader-hacanagent). When both factions cooperate, copying Hacan’s agent can help produce a commodity refresh and negotiated split. Sources: [SCPT 358, 4379.23–4380.13s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 4553.87–4555.17s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
- [Transparasteel Plating](../components.md#technology-tp) **conflicts-with** [Hyper Metabolism](../components.md#technology-hm). The guide presents these as alternative early green technologies, chosen by economy and tactical need. Sources: [SCPT 358, 2322.23–2326.51s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 2428.95–2434.81s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 4073.13–4076.89s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/); [SCPT 358, 4177.97–4184.39s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c01"></a>

- **Draft:** The action-card engine compounds over time: cards answer problems across movement, combat, economy, technology, and agendas, while Scheming lets Yssaril prune toward useful options. The hosts describe a tailored late-game toolkit, not a guaranteed win.
  Conditions: Best over a longer game; results still depend on cards, board, scoring pace, and player decisions. Compatibility: SCPT episode 358 (2024-07-03); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Podcast strategy opinion.
  Sources: [SCPT 358 2620–2628s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 2630–2634s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 2713–2715s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 2717–2719s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
  Components: [The Yssaril Tribes](yssaril.md), [Scheming](../components.md#ability-scheming), [Neural Motivator](../components.md#technology-nm)
<a id="claim-c02"></a>

- **Draft:** The opening has two carriers, a cruiser, two fighters, five infantry, and a home PDS. The hosts call this broadly useful but describe the early ground position as thin until mechs can be deployed.
  Conditions: Expand with the fleet while accounting for the action cards required to place mechs. Compatibility: SCPT episode 358 (2024-07-03); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: ASR proper nouns are noisy.
  Sources: [SCPT 358 808–814s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 814–819s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1512–1516s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1525–1528s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
  Components: [The Yssaril Tribes](yssaril.md), [Blackshade Infiltrator](../components.md#unit-yssaril-mech)
<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Neural Motivator is a natural starting technology: it draws an extra action card, and Scheming adds a card when drawing then permits a discard. That supports selection rather than a simple draw-and-keep pattern.
  Conditions: Most useful when there are weak cards to prune or several new choices; it does not promise a particular card. Compatibility: SCPT episode 358 (2024-07-03); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Rules text unchecked.
  Sources: [SCPT 358 829–830s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1154–1160s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1160–1164s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1190–1196s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1200–1207s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
  Components: [Neural Motivator](../components.md#technology-nm), [Scheming](../components.md#ability-scheming)
<a id="claim-c04"></a>

- **Draft:** Politics secondary is attractive because additional cards can build a large hand without the ordinary limit forcing Yssaril to prune down to seven. The hosts describe card draw as positive momentum.
  Conditions: Not an automatic follow; command tokens, timing, and card utility still matter. Compatibility: SCPT episode 358 (2024-07-03); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Informal hand-limit discussion.
  Sources: [SCPT 358 1326–1332s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1343–1346s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1356–1360s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
  Components: [Scheming](../components.md#ability-scheming), [Politics](../components.md#strategy-card-pok3politics)
<a id="claim-c05"></a>

- **Draft:** Stall Tactics converts an action-card discard into an action-phase stall without passing. Its use can also trigger mech deployment, giving the delay an additional payoff and an early deterrent.
  Conditions: Use when delaying is valuable and a mech can be deployed on a controlled planet. Compatibility: SCPT episode 358 (2024-07-03); expansion and ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Guide explanation is not a ruling.
  Sources: [SCPT 358 1026–1029s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1036–1039s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1488–1494s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1494–1499s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/) · [SCPT 358 1500–1503s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/358-super-yssaril-tribes-guide/)
